ai.description: This small frog (20–25 mm) is brown with a darker dorsal pattern. It features a pointed snout and elongated, slender digits. Males perform rhythmic foot-flagging displays to signal during breeding.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Nilgiri Dancing Frog is best distinguished by its unique habit of extending and flagging its hind legs, combined with a distinct, pointed snout and granular skin.
ai.habitat: The Nilgiri Dancing Frog inhabits the leaf litter and rocky stream banks of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 700 and 1,300 meters.
ai.behavior: To attract mates, male Nilgiri Dancing Frogs perform a unique "foot-flagging" display, extending and waving their hind legs to signal to rivals and potential partners.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus phyllophilus* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs in hidden nests constructed within stream-bed gravel and sand.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Nilgiri Dancing Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting streams in Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 700 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Nilgiri Dancing Frog emits a high-pitched, short "tink" sound repeated in rapid, irregular bursts, typically heard near fast-flowing forest streams.
